html:
SMTO-EXE-0243 — SMTO can't tell whether your Docker change happened

GUID: a286cb0c-d2eb-543c-a8bd-2131d7df1757
Slug: docker-operation-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO asked Docker to make a change, but lost track of the answer. The change may have happened, partly happened, or not happened at all.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to show the current containers, images or Compose project status on that Gateway, without changing anything. Looking at the current state shows whether the change already took effect.
  2. If SMTO can't reach the Gateway, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for it. A lost connection to the Gateway is a common reason the answer went missing.
  3. If the change is already there, stop. Only if it clearly did not happen, ask SMTO to make it again, and approve the new request if SMTO asks. Repeating a change that already happened can create duplicate containers or restart services a second time.

What success looks like

  • The Docker state shows your change exactly once, and nothing is duplicated.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't repeat the change just because this error appeared.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Docker change on the selected Gateway lost its trustworthy result (lost connection or response, a container exec without a final exit code, a build-cache record still present after removal, or reconciliation that could not confirm completion), so the effect is unknown.

What this means

  • An attempted Docker mutation lost its trustworthy result, container exec lacked a terminal exit result, cache removal remained observable or existing reconciliation could not establish completion. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • An attempted Docker mutation lost its trustworthy result, container exec lacked a terminal exit result, cache removal remained observable or existing reconciliation could not establish completion.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact Engine/registry objects, execution identity, known_completed facts and retained reconciliation result.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the selected Engine (docker.containers, docker.container, docker.images, docker.compose_ps) and any registry involved, using the receipt's object_id, known_completed and reconciliation fields. Establish whether the original effect occurred before authorizing any new mutation; never replay the original operation.
  • Inspect the selected Engine and registry state; do not replay an uncertain mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the selected Engine and registry state; do not replay an uncertain mutation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original effect is established before another mutation is authorized.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
